sections.h2: Which Trigg County offices matter for a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Every tax office sits in Cadiz, the county seat, and the county clerk's website lists the phone numbers for all of them. The clerk's real estate line is (270) 522-6661, and the office at 38 Main Street opens weekdays from 8:00 am until 4:00 pm.

  • Sheriff, (270) 522-6014: collects the current year's bills.
  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), (270) 522-3271: assigns values, takes exemption applications and holds the meeting that has to precede any appeal.
  • County clerk, (270) 522-6661: handles recording, marriage licenses and delinquent taxes. Vehicle titles and renewals use (270) 522-0217.
  • County attorney, (270) 522-4733: mails the notices that precede a delinquent tax sale.

The clerk also closes for the Trigg County Ham Festival each October. In 2026 that meant half of Thursday, October 8 and all of Friday, October 9, so plan payoff requests around festival week.

sections.h2: Why does Trigg County property differ from other Kentucky counties?
sections.html:
Water shapes everything here. Trigg covers 481 square miles, 40 of them water (8.3 percent), on the far southwest edge of Kentucky beside Lake Barkley. Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area, more than 170,000 acres with about 300 miles of natural shoreline on the peninsula between Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley, reaches into the county. Cadiz is known as the Antique Capital of Western Kentucky, and Lake Barkley State Resort Park and Prizer Point Marina pull visitors to the shore.

The legislature formed the county in 1820 from Christian and Caldwell counties and named it for Lt. Col. Stephen Trigg, killed at the Battle of Blue Licks in 1782. Lyon, Caldwell, Christian, Calloway and Marshall counties border it, along with Stewart County, Tennessee. Cerulean (partly in Christian County) is a census-designated place, and Golden Pond is listed as a ghost town. The county remained dry until voters narrowly approved off-premises alcohol sales in 2009.

Lake Barkley State Resort Park is known for a lodge billed as the largest wood-beam structure east of the Mississippi, and Prizer Point rents boats, kayaks and paddleboards and offers cabins and RV sites. The Janice Mason Art Museum occupies a restored downtown post office. Each October the Ham Festival fills Cadiz with food and entertainment.

Population topped 14,500 in 1910, sank to 8,620 by 1970 and was back at 14,061 in 2020. July 2025 is estimated at 14,512.

sections.h2: How many Trigg County homes sit empty or serve as second homes?
sections.html:
Counting units against households tells the story. The county has 7,733 housing units but 6,060 households, and the 2020 census called 23.4 percent of units vacant, the highest share among Spencer, Taylor, Todd and Trigg. Rentals stood empty at a rate of 11.7 percent. A county built around two large lakes can show that pattern, though the Census does not give the reason.

  • Owner-occupied homes carry a typical value of $207,700, and owners occupy 76.9 percent of units.
  • The usual rent is $803 and household income is $59,857.
  • Seniors make up 24.9 percent of residents, the largest share among the four counties, with a 2020 median age of 46.8.
  • No building permits were reported for 2025.
  • Poverty affects 13.9 percent of residents, and 19.6 percent under 65 have a disability.

With that many older owners, the homestead exemption is worth asking about early.

sections.h2: What does the Trigg County economy look like?
sections.html: Tourism and services carry the local numbers. The Census Bureau counted 231 employer establishments in 2023 with 2,202 employees, a 7.8 percent jump from 2022, the largest gain of the four counties. In 2022 retail sales were $130.9 million, lodging and restaurants took in $25.1 million and medical and social services $40.0 million. Only 51.1 percent of people over 16 are in the workforce, the thinnest share of the four counties, in line with the older age profile. The average trip to work takes 24.3 minutes.

sections.h2: How do Trigg County tax bills and penalties work?
sections.html:
The regular due date under state law falls at year end. Early payers by November 1 get a 2 percent discount; the printed amount applies through year end; January payments carry 5 percent; anything later carries 10 percent. If the state delays bills, the Department of Revenue can swap in an alternative schedule: two full months to pay after mailing, discount in month one, printed amount in month two, a 5 percent penalty for a month and 10 percent after.

Bills unpaid when the sheriff's period closes on April 15 go to the clerk as certificates of delinquency.

sections.h2: What was the 2026 Trigg County delinquent tax sale schedule?
sections.html:
The clerk runs one delinquent tax sale a year, at the end of July in the year after the taxes were due. The calendar for the 2025 bills, which has already run, shows the order of events.

Trigg County delinquent tax sale for the 2025 bills (source: Trigg County Clerk)
StepDate
List of certificates published in the Cadiz RecordJune 4, 2026
Registration deadline for buyers, close of businessJuly 2, 2026
Tax sale at the clerk's office, 38 Main Street, 9:00 amJuly 17, 2026

The list was also open for viewing at the clerk's office on weekdays and on the clerk's website. Owners could pay at the clerk any time before the sale; money that arrived afterward was returned. Some advertised bills were excluded under KRS 134.504(10)(b). Each year's dates and rules document appear on the clerk's delinquent tax page.

sections.h2: How can a Trigg County owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
The PVA's conference comes first, before or during the inspection period, and the roll stays open to view for two weeks in May. An owner who has been through the conference files with the county clerk on the next workday after that window.

The local board then convenes within roughly five weeks and can sit for up to five days. The board expects paper, such as lot and building details, insurance policies, what the house cost to build or comparable listings, and rejects an appeal without it. Separately, the PVA appraises most homes from nearby sales and walks each parcel at least every fourth year. Personal property that is taxable must be listed with the PVA between New Year's Day and May 15, and a later filing is treated as omitted.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Trigg County homestead exemption?
sections.html: A resident owner who is 65, or totally disabled, can deduct $49,100 from the assessment for 2025 and 2026, provided the house is owned, lived in and kept up on January 1. Applications go to the Trigg County PVA before December 31. Someone classified as totally disabled by an agency outside Kentucky renews every year. Veterans with a service-connected total disability and people found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security file once.

sections.h2: How do I settle Trigg County taxes when selling?
sections.html: Request the current payoff from the sheriff and ask the clerk if a certificate of delinquency exists. Under KRS 134.015 the January 1 owner carries that year's tax as a personal debt, and a delinquency lien can outlast a transfer by up to eleven years. When an investor bought the certificate at the July sale, the payoff goes to that investor.

faqs.q: Who collects current property tax in Trigg County?
faqs.a: The sheriff, at (270) 522-6014. After the April 15 cutoff the county clerk, (270) 522-6661, takes over unpaid bills.

faqs.q: When does the Trigg County clerk hold its delinquent tax sale?
faqs.a: Annually, near the end of July. The 2026 sale ran on July 17, 2026, at 9:00 am, and later dates are posted on the clerk's delinquent tax page.

faqs.q: Can I still pay after my Trigg County bill is advertised?
faqs.a: Yes, up to the sale. The clerk's office at 38 Main Street accepts delinquent payments before that date and returns any that arrive afterward.

faqs.q: What is the Trigg County homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: $49,100 in assessed value for 2025 and 2026. Seniors and totally disabled owners can file with the PVA at (270) 522-3271 before the year ends.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Trigg County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Yes. Closing clears the lien out of your sale money, so collect written payoffs from the sheriff and the clerk beforehand.
